title: Permutations
source: canonical Permutations concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of distinct integers. Return every ordering of those values: all n! permutations. Sort the list of permutations ascending so the output is deterministic.
constraints: every value in nums is distinct

examples.explanation: Three values arrange in six orders.
One value has exactly one ordering.

hints: Build orders position by position: at each step, any not-yet-used value may come next.
A used flag per value keeps each recursion branch from repeating a value.
When the built order reaches full length, record a copy; backtrack by unmarking and popping.
solution: Backtracking with a used-mask: at each position try every unused value, record the order when complete, and undo. n! orderings fall out in ascending order when the values start sorted. O(n * n!) time, O(n) recursion depth.
solutionCode:
def permutations(nums):
    values = sorted(nums)
    result = []
    used = [False] * len(values)
    current = []
    def walk():
        if len(current) == len(values):
            result.append(list(current))
            return
        for i in range(len(values)):
            if not used[i]:
                used[i] = True
                current.append(values[i])
                walk()
                current.pop()
                used[i] = False
    walk()
    return result
